title: The buzzard roof at the Majestic and disillusion with idols in New York
summary: Cobb recalls sitting in the segregated roof of Houston's Majestic Theater to see the big bands, then finding the same stars short of money in New York, which made him begin to save.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But I need them like I need another hole in the head, Ellen, because I have to make my own way. They made me do this. I had guys that come down to Houston that I admired, respected, and I'm in the buzzard group. You know what the buzzard group is? In the Majestic Theater where Blacks had to go to catch the Cab Callaways, the Lucky Millinders, the Jimmie Luncefords, you listen to me, unless I
went backstage, and the only band I went backstage on was Jimmy Lunceford's because of Joe Thomas.
What do you mean, the buzzards?
I call it the buzzard roof.

MR. COBB: Roof, because that's where it was. It was in the roof, right next to the ceiling upstairs, as high as the theater was. That's where we had to sit, and we went in a different entrance. And all the acts on the show, man, was first class. Oh, I just enjoyed this, and I wasn't (inaudible). I got to New York and saw these same people that I admired bagging for a couple of dollars. You hear me talking to you. You don't believe it.

I'm at the Apollo Theater. Here I am admiring them. Here they come and asking me for some money, and I'm working as a side man in Lionel Hampton, and they'd starve in Houston. But in New York there was nothing. I didn't know that. See how you can be deceived and be disillusioned? And this is when I made up my mind. I said, this what it takes to deceive

people and be disillusioned. I'm going to start saving. Why, I don't want to be in this position no time down the road, and I started to prepare for (inaudible). I told you yesterday I took sick, had the spinal operation, had to go back and have it over, and when I come out of the hospital and I'd never gone to Ben Barr's office for the petty cash or nothing, I had one $700.00 left out of my savings and took part of that and bought a uniform for my band to start over again.
